successors.text: Ternate and its remaining dependencies, annexed by the Dutch in 1914

ledger.x: 1257: Momole Cico founds the Ternate kingdom.

c. 1400s: Ternate takes the Sula Islands and Seram. 'In the 1400s, Ternate also conquered neighboring islands such as the Sula Islands and Seram Island.' The page gives the century only; 1450 is the mid-point (page silent on the year); what the page calls Seram is drawn as its western part.
1486: Zainal Abidin makes the kingdom a sultanate.
1522: the Portuguese begin their fort on Ternate.

ledger.cp: Ternate's eastern dependencies (eastern Sulawesi, Ambon-Seram, Banda, Solor, Timor, southern Mindanao, Papuan Islands)

ledger.x: 1575: the Portuguese are expelled from Ternate.
1583: Babullah dies and the peak ends.
ledger.cp: Ternate's eastern dependencies (eastern Sulawesi, Ambon-Seram, Banda, Solor, Timor, southern Mindanao, Papuan Islands)

ledger.x: 1606: the Spanish take the fort of Ternate.
1656: the Ambon Quarter passes to the Dutch.
1801: the British and Tidore take Ternate.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1802: the Dutch regain their Maluku posts after the Peace of Amiens (Tidore page: 'the following year').

ledger.x: 1817: Ternate returns to Dutch control after the British occupation of 1810.

wars.name: Ternate-Portuguese war and siege of Fort Kastela
wars.outcome: The Ternatans 'expelled the Portuguese in 1575 after a five-year siege'; the garrison 'forced to capitulate to Sultan Babullah'.

wars.name: Spanish capture of Ternate and the Dutch return
wars.outcome: Spain captured the fort in 1606 and took Sultan Said to Manila; the Dutch, allied with Ternate, built a fort at Malayo in 1607; the Spanish, allied with Tidore, 'abandoned Ternate and Tidore in 1663'.

wars.name: VOC subordination of Ternate and Tidore (1650s)
wars.outcome: 'the subordination of Ternate and Tidore in the 1650s' (Maluku page); the Ambon Quarter governed from Hoamoal 'up to 1656'; the 1683 treaty made Ternate a Dutch vassal.

wars.name: British capture of Ternate (1801 and 1810)
wars.outcome: British (with Tidore) took Ternate in 1801, returned it after the Peace of Amiens; British forces seized it again in 1810 and returned it in 1817.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for any date; island groups are drawn as discs.
